name: Labcorp
description: Labcorp runs clinical laboratories that test patient samples ordered by physicians and hospitals (Diagnostics, 78 percent of 2025 revenue) and also sells laboratory testing to drug and device makers running clinical trials (Biopharma Laboratory Services, 22 percent). The Diagnostics side is billed per test to insurers, health-system clients, government programs and patients; its 2025 revenue was $10.9B in a US clinical lab industry the company estimates at more than $80B. The biopharma side is paid by pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical-device and diagnostics companies and contract research organizations, and 59 percent of its revenue comes from outside the US. Labcorp has a Spin-off of Fortrea in its history and a transition services agreement with it (10-K). It pays a dividend of $0.72 a quarter and has been buying back shares (1.7 million shares for $452M in H1 2026) while acquiring lab businesses (about $528.6M net of cash in H1 2026).

gics.note: SEC SIC code 8071 (Services-Medical Laboratories). Same sub-industry label as Quest Diagnostics and CVS Health in the source. Labcorp is 78% patient-testing (Dx) and 22% drug-development lab services for pharma (BLS), so its second segment does not resemble a health-care service at all.

hq.note: 358 South Main Street, Burlington, NC 27215 (FY2025 10-K cover)

employees.note: About 71,000 employees across 17 countries serving clients in about 100 countries (FY2025 10-K); as-of date assumed to be fiscal year-end, text does not state a date in the extract read

businessLines.name: Diagnostics (Dx)
businessLines.shareBasis: Share of revenue per the 10-K revenue table (78% of $13,951.7M). Share of profit = 1,779.9 / 2,278.4 segment operating income.
businessLines.how: Physician and patient test orders are billed per test to whoever pays: third-party payers (37% of company revenue in 2025), health-system and other clients billed directly (23%), patients (10%) and Medicare and Medicaid (8%). Contracts with managed-care organizations set the price, and volume follows test orders.
businessLines.description: Routine testing and specialty/esoteric testing for patients, through patient service centers, physician offices, hospitals and health-system outreach; nearly all revenue is US.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating income before general corporate and unallocated expenses ($482.2M), amortization and restructuring; FY2024 $1,606.3M; Q2 2026 $522.6M vs $482.8M

businessLines.marketShare: Company estimates the US clinical lab testing industry at more than $80B in 2025 (10-K); Dx revenue of $10.9B is therefore at most about 13-14% of it (computed; Dx is nearly all US)

businessLines.name: Biopharma Laboratory Services (BLS)
businessLines.how: Drug and device sponsors and contract research organizations sign contracts for laboratory work on their trials and research programs and pay for the services delivered; the 10-K says contracts with several promises are allocated by price list. Revenue depends on customer trial and research activity; about 41% of BLS revenue is US and 59% is from other countries (10-K).
businessLines.description: Central Laboratory (testing for clinical trials) and ED (Early Development Research Laboratories) services for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device and diagnostics companies and contract research organizations, including support through regulatory approval.

brands.name: Empire City Laboratories and Parkview Health Systems outreach business
brands.segment: Dx acquisitions closed in the six months ended 2026-06-30
brands.share: Total acquisition consideration of about $528.6M net of cash for all businesses acquired in the period; individual sizes not extracted
